composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

normalizeAddress:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerAddress
  next: validate

validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  next: validatePostcode

validatePostcode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidatePostcode
  next: validateRegistrationDate

validateRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateRegistrationDate
  next: normalizeTelephone

normalizeTelephone:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerTelephone
  next: normalizeEmail

normalizeEmail:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerEmail
  next: rejectDisposableEmail

rejectDisposableEmail:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectDisposableEmailDomain
  next: checkCityCapacity

checkCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkDailyLimit

checkDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkIdentityUnique

# Duplicate check: runs after the deterministic householdId is assigned. Rejects a full
# identityKey (telephone|email|householdId) match always, and a household (same householdId,
# i.e. same lastName+postcode) match unless the request sets sharesHousehold. Before save so
# the new owner is matched only against existing owners.
checkIdentityUnique:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerIdentityUnique
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignPossibleDuplicate

# Soft-match: only reached when not a hard duplicate. A declared household member
# (sharesHousehold) is never flagged; otherwise a lastName+postcode match with a different
# telephone is still created but flagged possibleDuplicate with the match id.
assignPossibleDuplicate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignPossibleDuplicate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCustomerCode

assignCustomerCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignNamesakeCount

assignNamesakeCount:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignMembershipNumber

assignMembershipNumber:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignMembershipNumber
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: bulkSignupWarning

bulkSignupWarning:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignBulkSignupWarning
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: householdMemberCount

householdMemberCount:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHouseholdMemberCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

## Summary

I implemented customerCode de-duplication in `AssignCustomerCode.java` (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/AssignCustomerCode.java`).

**Change:** The step now injects `OwnerRepository` (resolved by type, per the OfficeFloor function-injection convention) alongside the existing `@Val Owner`. It computes the base `<REGION>-<HASH8>` code as before, then:

1. Collects the set of existing owners' `customerCode` values via `ownerRepository.findAll()`.
2. If the base code collides, appends `-<n>` starting at `n=2` and incrementing until unique (`-2`, `-3`, …), assigning the smallest available `n`.

This runs before `save` (as it already did in the pipeline), so the new owner is matched only against owners already present. The dedup happens before `AssignMembershipNumber` and the check-digit steps, so those derive correctly from the final de-duplicated code.

The Cp41 collision test passes along with all other tests that depend on `customerCode` (Cp09, Cp14, Cp16, Cp31, Cp32, Cp21), and the full suite is green.
